focus: Phases 009-skills and 010-conversations: reference files implementing the same thing, what to lift or mirror, where the plan differs and which side the evidence supports, and the failures the plan does not yet guard against.
noveltyJustification: 8 of 9 findings are new to the packet and 1 confirms an existing plan rule, so the ratio is 8.5/9 rounded down to 0.90.
keyQuestions: Which reference files implement the 009 skills surface and what does the plan not guard against?
Which reference files implement the 010 conversations surface and where does the plan differ?
answeredQuestions: 009 has no scan of a loaded skill body, no per-skill tool declaration, no symlink refusal, and deliberately no scope precedence.
010's reference conversation is a front for a task thread, its prompt section is conditional on holding the tool, and its retired-tool rule is one line the plan should adopt in 013.
ruledOut: A scope-precedence ladder for 009: the plan has one tree and one name, so the reference's five roots solve a problem the plan does not have.
A task-thread handoff for 010: the plan's conversation is the run and its Problem Statement already names the limit.
A never-only-a-reaction rule for 010: the plan has no reactions and already refuses a blank line.

findings.label: 009: the reference scans a skill body for supply-chain hazards (bidi and zero-width code points, hard-coded credentials, escaping resource paths block; agent-addressed text and fetch-and-exec pipelines warn) while the plan scans only the draft for secret literals and never scans a loaded body, so a bidi override in a skill body goes straight into the prompt as instructions.

009: the reference parses an allowed-tools frontmatter key per skill and the plan has no per-skill tool declaration, so 007 filters per bot where a per-skill declaration would be the narrower grant and has a place to land in 007's per-run filtered config.

009: the reference pins an installed document by a rendered-document digest and the plan pins a proposal by the SHA-256 of the bytes as read, two independent designs reaching the same staged-write pin, and the reference's own note that a rendered digest differs from a bundled digest is the trap the plan avoids.

009: the reference carries a five-root scope precedence for discovery and the plan resolves one name against one tree, and the evidence supports the plan because a precedence ladder is a multi-root product's problem that the plan does not have.

009: the reference bounds a resource read by traversal, symlink, size and UTF-8 while the plan closes traversal through the name grammar and bounds the body by bytes, leaving a symlinked SKILL.md unrefused so the byte cap measures the wrong file.

010: the reference's conversation is a front for a task thread it delegates into, links to, follows up on and stops, while the plan's conversation is the run itself, so the reference's conversation survives the work and the plan's is a log of runs.

010: the reference retired its react tool and kept the name so an old transcript still draws, and the plan has no retirement rule even though 006's action kinds and 007's apps introduce names a later phase may retire, so 013 should own the one-line rule keep the name, stop offering it, keep drawing it.

010: the reference makes its conversation prompt section conditional on holding the tool because a routine or check-in turn holds none, while the plan adds the section to the one prompt builder that 002's routine runs also read, so a routine prompt would tell a bot to answer a person who is not there.

010: the reference's never-only-a-reaction failure is already covered by the plan in its analogous form, because the plan appends the run's exit reason to an empty reply so the line is never blank, which is the same rule for a text-only client.
